title: Zero-trust Segmentation & mTLS checklist for Private Deployments
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic zero-trust network segmentation pattern for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem), a set of hardened firewall rule templates, a concise mTLS setup + rotation plan, an RBAC v2 mapping for network operations, and recommended audit-log schema and SIEM export options. Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, security reviewers, and customer infra teams preparing a Private deployment.

Scope and goals:
- Ensure least-privilege network paths between control plane, data plane (model servers), and administrative tooling.
- Provide reproducible firewall/security-group templates for AWS and GCP.
- Standardize mTLS bootstrap and certificate rotation guidance for service-to-service auth.
- Define RBAC v2 roles relevant to network config and evidence needs.
- Define a minimal audit log schema suitable for SIEM ingestion and evidence automation.

High-level pattern (recommended): hub-and-spoke with enforcement plane
- Hub (shared services): logging, SIEM forwarders, secrets manager (customer KMS/HSM), bastion jump hosts (restricted), and transit gateway / cloud router.
- Spokes: workload VPCs for control-plane components, runtime GPU clusters, observability pipeline.
- Enforcement plane: centrally managed firewall appliances (cloud NVA or customer FW), and a policy engine (OPA/Gatekeeper or vendor).

ASCII diagram (simplified):
  +---------------------------+       +----------------+
  |   Customer Transit Hub    |<----->|  SIEM / ELK    |
  |  (transit gw, secrets)    |       |  (forwarder)   |
  +----+--------+-----+-------+       +----------------+
       |        |     |
       |        |     +---> Control-plane (redwood-control-vpc)
       |        +---------> Runtime GPU VPC (redwood-runtime-vpc)
       +-----------------> Observability VPC (redwood-observ-vpc)

Segmentation rules (principles):
- Default deny on inter-spoke traffic. Only explicitly allow routes through the transit hub for required services (e.g., SIEM, secrets, licensing).
- Use private endpoints (VPC endpoints / Private Service Connect) for control-plane APIs.
- Enforce egress filtering: deny outbound to internet except via vetted NAT or proxy with TLS inspection where required.
- Enforce host-based firewall (iptables/nftables) on model servers to limit lateral movement even within subnets.
- All inter-service traffic must be authenticated with mTLS and traceable via request IDs that appear in audit logs.

Firewall rule templates (examples)
- AWS Security Group (conceptual):
  - Name: sg-redwood-runtime-control-plane
  - Inbound:
    - TCP 443 from sg-redwood-control-plane (mTLS API)
    - TCP 10250 from sg-sre-bastion (k8s admin port, locked down)
    - ICMP from monitoring IP range (for health checks)
  - Outbound:
    - TCP 443 to VPC endpoints: secretsmanager/KMS/ssm
    - TCP 9200/12201 to observability-forwarder (only to forwarder IPs)
  - Notes: avoid wide CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 egress; prefer endpoint-specific allow-listing.

- GCP Firewall (conceptual):
  - Name: fw-redwood-runtime-egress
  - Direction: EGRESS, Priority: 1000
  - Deny all egress to 0.0.0.0/0 (action: deny)
  - Allow TCP 443 to private service connect endpoints and to defined SIEM forwarder IPs
  - Allow UDP 123 to NTP servers

- On-prem bare-metal pattern: VLANs + ACLs
  - Separate VLAN for management, compute, and storage
  - ACLs on leaf switches: management VLAN -> jump host only, compute VLAN -> control API endpoints only

mTLS bootstrap & rotation (recommended steps)
1) Root PKI: customer-managed Root CA or HSM-backed key in KMS. Redwood can accept externally issued certs or act as an intermediate only if customer allows.
2) Issuance: short-lived leaf certs (TTL 7-30 days) issued via automated CSR flow (cert-manager on k8s or vault-pki for VM-based).
3) Bootstrapping: initial node provisioning uses a one-time bootstrap token tied to a short-lived cert signed by an onboarding CA.
4) Rotation: automate renewal at 25% of TTL (e.g., renew at day 2 for 7-day certs). Use rolling restart without traffic blackholing; employ TLS session resumption/KV cache warmers to avoid cold start.
5) Revocation: maintain ocsp/CRL endpoints. Use short TTLs to minimize blast radius.
6) Best practice: require mutual cert validation + host SAN checks + SPIFFE identities for workload-level scoping.

RBAC v2 mapping (network-focused roles)
- network-admin: can modify firewall rules, route tables, and transit configuration (assign to platform-networking group).
- network-auditor: read-only access to network config, VPC flow logs, and audit logs.
- secrets-operator: can rotate certs and access PKI endpoints, limited to the namespace for cert management.
- bastion-operator: manage jump hosts and ephemeral access sessions (TACACS/SSO integration).
- ci-cd-agent-network: limited policy allowing ephemeral provisioning of load balancers and target group registration via a restricted service account.

Implementation notes for RBAC v2:
- Ensure role changes and policy updates themselves are logged and included in the audit stream.
- Tie roles to SSO groups and short-lived session credentials where possible.

Audit log schema (minimal recommended fields)
Each network event should include a single-line JSON object (concise and indexed by SIEM):
- timestamp: ISO8601 (UTC)
- tenant_id: customer or account id
- request_id: globally unique request identifier (UUID)
- source: IP or service identity (e.g., spiffe://cluster/ns/service)
- destination: IP/service/port
- protocol: tcp/udp/http
- action: allow/deny/modify
- policy_id: id of policy or rule evaluated
- result: success/failure + HTTP code if applicable
- actor: user/service principal that initiated change (email or service account)
- changed_by_ticket: optional link to Jira/ChangeID that approved network change
- bytes_in/bytes_out: numerical
- flow_id: flow sampling id (if available)
- host_agent_version: version of sidecar or agent reporting
- geo: optional (customer-configured)

Example single-line audit: 
{"timestamp":"2026-01-18T13:12:05Z","tenant_id":"acct-7781","request_id":"7f6b9a2a-9c3b-4d2e-8a91-0f2a6d5c1b3e","source":"10.20.5.12","destination":"10.40.1.4:443","protocol":"tcp","action":"allow","policy_id":"fw-rt-327","result":"success","actor":"svc:model-proxy@redwood","bytes_in":1480,"bytes_out":22000,"host_agent_version":"v0.9.3"} 

SIEM export recommendations
- Preferred transport: TLS-encrypted JSON over TCP (or HEC for Splunk). Avoid plain syslog where possible.
- For Splunk HEC: use HEC tokens scoped to a forwarder role; tag events with tenant_id and source_type=redwood_network.
- For Elastic: use Beats or a secure Logstash pipeline. Enrich logs with geo and tenant metadata at ingestion time.
- CEF/LEEF: only for legacy integrations; map policy_id to deviceEventClassId and include request_id as extension field to enable stitching.

Example Splunk HEC mapping (text):
- index: redwood_network
- sourcetype: redwood:network:audit
- fields to send: timestamp (as _time), tenant_id, request_id, source, destination, action, policy_id, actor, result

Evidence automation & playbook (automated artifacts for compliance review)
Goal: produce a reproducible evidence bundle per change window or policy update that contains: audit logs (filtered), current firewall config, running cert inventory, and a playback of policy evaluation for sampled flows.
1) Trigger: on policy change (PR merged) or scheduled (daily snapshot).
2) Gather:
   - Query audit logs for window and export (JSONL)
   - Pull firewall rules and route tables (cloud APIs)
   - Pull certificate inventory from cert-manager/vault (subject, SAN, expiry)
   - Collect VPC flow logs (sampled window)
3) Package: compress to signed artifact (zip + detached signature), push to customer-approved evidence bucket (immutable storage)
4) Index: register artifact in internal evidence index with metadata (policy_id, window, signer, hash)
5) Retention: follow customer SLA (e.g., 365 days for regulated customers)

Automation script snippets (pseudocode for evidence snapshot):
- aws: awslogs->s3 export -> sign -> upload
- gcp: gcloud logging read -> gsutil cp -> sign -> upload

Hardening checklist (operational tasks; mark status during onboarding)
- [ ] Enable VPC flow logs for every spoke (central collector bucket).
- [ ] Centralize audit logs to SIEM; no local-only retention.
- [ ] Enforce mTLS for all inter-service requests (fail closed).
- [ ] Implement host-based firewall rules on all model servers.
- [ ] Configure egress filtering and NAT / proxy with allow-list.
- [ ] Rotate root CA certs per policy and enforce short-lived leaf certs.
- [ ] Apply RBAC v2 roles; record approval tickets for admin role grants.
- [ ] Schedule daily evidence snapshot during deployment windows.
- [ ] Configure alerting on policy evaluation rejects > threshold.
- [ ] Test SIEM ingestion and run a mock audit with playbook.

Operational runbook snippets (incident quick steps):
- If suspicious lateral movement detected:
  1) Isolate affected subnet in transit hub (apply deny-all egress to offender IPs).
  2) Pull recent audit logs filtered by request_id and source IP and push to quarantine evidence bucket.
  3) Rotate affected leaf certs and revoke via CRL/OCSP if needed.
  4) Open ticket with network-admin group and attach evidence bundle.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize schema mapping for vendor SIEMs (Splunk vs. Elastic vs. Sumologic) — need to confirm field names and sampling strategy.
- Decide on default TTL for leaf certs (7 vs 30 days) based on customer operational tolerance.
- Evaluate using SPIFFE/SPIRE for identity vs. cert-manager for easier on-prem lifecycle.
- Add automated compliance report generator (PDF + hash) that signs the evidence artifact with HSM.

Notes & references (internal):
- See confluence:PD-NETWORK-ZT-arch-v2 for full diagrams and terraform modules.
- See JIRA:PDP-908 for rollout checklist and migration tasks.
- Security contact: security-oncall@redwood.example (use in incident workflows).

Revision history: 
- 2024-10-12: initial draft by Avery Chen
- 2025-03-15: added SIEM mapping and RBAC v2 roles (review comments from Leah)
- 2026-02-14: refined mTLS rotation section and added evidence automation steps (Samir)

This doc is an operational working draft — expect follow-up PRs with concrete terraform modules and example cert-manager manifests.
